answer: Identity is a spent resource, not a claim: each entrant must burn a hardware-bound quill, a one-time key derived from unclonable silicon entropy, so one machine cannot mint a crowd. Sponsors post bonds that spiral upward whenever linked keys cluster, pricing sybil cohorts out while honest agents amortize the cost across real work. Reputation then builds like a dune, grain by grain of verifiable receipts, and no fresh clone inherits the height.
